abstract_text:
PROJECT SUMMARY
Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) are important mediators of neuronal excitability through their
participation in action potential generation and propagation, neurotransmitter release, and dendritic excitability.
Consequently, each of the alpha subunits of the four VGSCs that are markedly expressed in the CNS (SCN1A,
SCN2A, SCN3A, and SCN8A) are associated with severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE).
Patients living with DEE often have a constellation of phenotypes, spanning many seizure types and abnormal
epileptiform EEG activity, as well as developmental delays including cognitive deficits, sleep disturbances,
behavioral abnormalities, and motor impairments. Current therapies for SCN3A-DEE address symptoms and are
not sufficiently effective. Accordingly, there is a significant need to better understand the etiology of SCN3A-DEE
and to develop improved therapeutics based on this understanding. SCN3A is highly enriched in the developing
fetal brain across progenitor populations, nascent neurons, and developing glia. Pathogenic variants in SCN3A
have been identified in patients with DEE presenting with malformations of cortical development, which are most
often gain-of-function. Collectively, these observations point to an early developmental origin of SCN3A-DEE –
possibly prior to the establishment of action potential generation or synaptic transmission. Recent work from
colleagues demonstrates pathogenic variants influence mature neuron functions, such as action potential
generation; how VGSCs including SCN3A influence early cellular activities in neural precursors and nascent
neurons and glia leading to impaired cortical development is not well understood. Here we propose to use human
cellular models of SCN3A-DEE to interrogate mechanisms of corticogenesis in three Aims. Aim 1 will
mechanistically interrogate the emergence of electrical activity in excitable and non-excitable cell types using
Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiology to understand the relationship between activity, brain development, and the
cellular impairments in the SCN3A models. Aim 2 will use pharmacological tools and SCN3A-DEE and knockout
models to probe mechanisms of VGSC-mediated effects on cell migration. Aim 3 will evaluate, using human
cellular models, three orthogonal therapeutic approaches for correction of cortical malformation and excitability
phenotypes. Therapeutic approaches include RNA knockdown of SCN3A, selective pharmacological inhibition
of SCN3A or VGSC currents, and delivery of synthetic peptides that act as VGSC open state blockers.
Successful completion of this proposal will 1) define cellular and physiological mechanisms of SCN3A-DEE in
the developing cortex, 2) generate fundamental knowledge of the role of VGSCs in cortical development and 3)
test three innovative therapeutic strategies for SCN3A-DEE.
project_title: Mechanisms and Treatment of SCN3A-Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
phr_text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE
The proposed research will interrogate pathogenic mechanisms in a human cellular model of developmental and
epileptic encephalopathy. The project will comprehensively determine which cell types are affected and how their
development is impaired leading to disease. This project will also evaluate several pre-clinical therapeutic
approaches in human cellular models for improved treatment of developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
